question: Should core permanently reserve the top-level `openclaw auth` namespace for model-auth shortcuts even though plugins are documented to register root command groups?
rationale: The code can implement either direction, but choosing namespace ownership and compatibility behavior changes the public CLI/plugin contract and cannot be inferred safely from tests or the contributor's alias proposal.

options.title: Keep auth under models
options.body: Retain `openclaw models auth list` as the single canonical command and close or rework this alias PR so plugin root namespace remains available.

options.title: Reserve the auth root
options.body: Explicitly designate `auth` as core-owned, document collision and upgrade behavior, add plugin-compatibility tests, and require live proof before merging.

recommendation.title: Keep auth under models
recommendation.body: Retain `openclaw models auth list` as the single canonical command and close or rework this alias PR so plugin root namespace remains available.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on plugin CLI registration makes this the strongest available owner for the root-command namespace decision.
